name: as.Date.yearmon
title: An Index Class for Monthly Data

origin.description: Date at a fraction of the way through a month.

arguments.name: frac
arguments.text: Number from 0 to 1. Zero is the first day of the month and one is the last day.

origin.details: The year is floor(x + 0.001) and the month is floor(12 * (x - year) + 1.501). The last day is 32 days after the first, minus the day-of-month of that later date. The result is (1 - frac) times the first day plus frac times the last day, in days since 1970-01-01.
origin.example:
x <- as.yearmon(2000 + seq(0, 13)/12)
cat(paste(as.character(as.Date(x)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
cat(paste(as.character(as.Date(x, frac = 1)), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Date at a fraction of the way through a month.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A Yearmon, or the numeric values a yearmon stores.

arguments.name: frac
arguments.text: Number from 0 to 1, recycled to the length of x. Zero is the first day and one is the last day.

translation.details: The returned RDate.days are days since 1970-01-01. frac 0 is the first of the month. The last day follows the R rule: 32 days after the first, minus that date's day of the month. February 2000 ends on the 29th.
translation.example:
import math
import numpy as np
from zoo.yearmon import as_date_yearmon, as_yearmon, civil_from_days
x = as_yearmon(2000 + np.arange(14) / 12)
def iso(dates):
    parts = []
    for day in dates.days:
        y, m, d = civil_from_days(math.trunc(float(day)))
        parts.append(f"{y:04d}-{m:02d}-{d:02d}")
    return " ".join(parts)
print(iso(as_date_yearmon(x)))
print(iso(as_date_yearmon(x, frac=1)))
